title: Design exercise: SAA-1.3-S07
scenario: Larkspur Payroll Services encrypts customer data with 320 symmetric customer-managed keys and signs payslip files with 6 asymmetric signing keys; it also runs 30 public TLS certificates on its load balancers, 26 issued through AWS Certificate Manager with DNS validation and 4 imported from a banking partner's authority. Policy requires every key to change its cryptographic material at least annually without application changes, and after a suspected exposure last year, to be able to change a key's material within the same day. Certificates must never expire in production. Two platform engineers maintain everything and want the least ongoing manual work.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
No application change or redeployment is allowed when key material changes
Data already encrypted must remain readable after every change of key material
The two platform engineers want the least ongoing manual work

rubric.label: Each of the 6 signing keys has a stated annual replacement path that meets the no-application-change rule, and the record says why the symmetric keys' approach does not apply to them
The 4 imported certificates have an explicit renewal or replacement path

constraint_reason: Mapped as design_exercise to complete skill coverage when no dedicated live lab step exists
